text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and can not vouch for their accuracy.
- Union leaders have called on striking local government workers in the southern town of Livingstone to call off a strike that has crippled social services in Zambia's tourist capital.
- Some 100 Zairean refugees have crossed the border into Zambia in north western Zambia, bringing the number of recent arrivals from the trouble-torn country to around 300.
- Lusaka high court judge Kabazo Chanda on Tuesday ordered the release of 53 suspects, most of them facing aggravated robbery charges, who have been held without trial since 1992.
- Cholera has broken out in the southern agricultural town of Mazabuka, claiming four lives.
- Prospective investors to Zambia will have to undergo mandatory environmental impact assessment studies before undertaking their projects, environment minister William Harrington said.
- Two South African pilots on Tuesday pleaded not guilty to flouting Zambia's aviation laws by failing to communicate their approach to air traffic controllers.
